name: Full Groom
summary: Bath, blow-dry, clip & style, nails & ears — the complete package.
metaDescription: Full dog grooming in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — bath, blow-dry, clip and style, nails and ears. Small from £40, medium £50, large or doodles £60.
body: A full groom is what most owners book and what most dogs need every six to eight weeks. It's the works: a careful pre-groom check, a warm bath with shampoo and conditioner matched to your dog's coat type, a thorough towel-and-blow-dry, a clip-and-scissor finish to whatever length you like, nails trimmed, ears cleaned and a final brush-out before your dog goes home.

Most full grooms take between one-and-a-half and three hours, depending on size and coat condition. We work at your dog's pace — not the clock's. There are no shared dryers, no other dogs in the room, and no rush to fit the next appointment in. A cockapoo who needs a break to sniff around the salon gets one.

If your dog hasn't been groomed in a long time, or the coat is heavily matted, the kindest thing is sometimes to clip down to a short, healthy length and let it grow back properly. We'll always talk you through it before we pick up the clippers, and we'll never carry on with a groom that's becoming stressful for your dog.

Pricing is by size and coat type: small dogs (terriers, shih-tzus, bichons) from £40, medium dogs (cockapoos, mini schnauzers, cocker spaniels) from £50, and large dogs or heavy-coated doodles (labradoodles, goldendoodles, retrievers) from £60. Heavy matting, anxious behaviour or unusually long gaps between grooms may add a little to the time and the price — we'll always confirm before we start.

faqs.q: How often should I book a full groom?
faqs.a: For most coats, every 6–8 weeks. Doodles and continuous-growth breeds (poodles, schnauzers, bichons) usually need 6 weeks; smoother coats can stretch to 8. Going much longer than 10 weeks risks matting that costs more to put right than the groom itself.

faqs.q: Do you do specific breed styles or lengths?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what you'd like — a teddy-bear cockapoo, a schnauzer in breed standard, a shorter summer cut — and we'll work to it. We'll also flag honestly if your dog's coat or skin can't take what you've asked for.

faqs.q: What does the price actually include?
faqs.a: Bath with breed-appropriate shampoo, towel and blow-dry, full body clip and scissor finish, face and feet tidy, nail trim, ear clean and a final brush-out. Nothing's a hidden add-on.

faqs.q: Will my dog be on their own or with other dogs?
faqs.a: On their own. We only ever have one dog in the salon at a time. No kennels, no waiting.

name: Puppy First Groom
summary: A gentle, reassuring introduction (up to ~6 months). Sets your pup up for a lifetime of stress-free grooming.
metaDescription: Gentle puppy first groom in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — calm 45-60 minute intro for pups up to 6 months. Sets your puppy up for stress-free grooming.
body: A puppy's first grooming experience matters more than people realise. Done gently, it teaches a young dog that the salon is a friendly place — somewhere they'll be calm and confident for the rest of their life. Done badly (or with a queue of barking adults in earshot), it can take years to undo.

The puppy first groom at Keith's K9 Care is a slower, calmer version of a normal session. Usually 45 to 60 minutes. We start with a sniff-around so your puppy can investigate the room. Then we introduce the sounds — clippers running near (but not on) them, the warm hum of the dryer at a distance — and reward each calm response with treats. Only when your puppy is settled do we move to a gentle bath, a light tidy of face, paws and rear, and a careful first nail trim.

Most puppies can have their first groom from around 12 weeks — after their second vaccination — but it's worth a quick chat first. We'll ask about coat type, breed, and how they handle new noises at home, and pick the right moment.

Follow-up puppy grooms (the second and subsequent visits up to ~6 months) build on the first. Puppy intro groom: from £25. Follow-up puppy groom: from £30. Cheaper than a full groom because we keep them shorter and lower-intensity by design — the goal is a confident adult dog, not a perfect cut.

faqs.q: When can my puppy have their first groom?
faqs.a: Usually any time after their second vaccination (around 12 weeks). The earlier we can introduce gentle handling, water and the sound of clippers, the easier every groom for the rest of their life.

faqs.q: What happens if my puppy gets upset?
faqs.a: We stop, take a break, give them a treat and try again — at their pace. There's no rule that says a groom has to finish in one session. Sometimes the best thing we can do is leave a bit until next time.

faqs.q: Can I stay with my puppy for the first appointment?
faqs.a: If you'd like to, yes — especially for the meet-and-sniff at the start. Most puppies actually settle better once their owner is in the other room, but you're welcome to be there if you'd rather.

faqs.q: Should my puppy be tired before the groom?
faqs.a: A short walk beforehand can help — but don't exhaust them. A puppy that's a bit calm-and-content settles best. Avoid feeding them within an hour of the appointment.

faqs.q: What should I bring?
faqs.a: A vaccination card the first time, a familiar treat if they have a favourite, and your phone for the proud post-groom photo. That's it.

name: Bath & Tidy
summary: Bath, blow-dry, brush, nails & tidy — the in-between visit between full grooms. Great for short coats and quick freshen-ups.
metaDescription: Bath and tidy dog grooming in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — bath, blow-dry, brush, nails and tidy. Small from £30, medium £40, large or doodles £50.
body: A bath and tidy is the lighter, quicker option between full grooms. Perfect for short-coated breeds, dogs who've been on a muddy walk, or anyone whose coat doesn't yet need a full clip but could really do with a clean and a tidy round the face, feet and rear.

We bathe with a breed-appropriate shampoo, towel and blow-dry properly (no damp dogs going home), brush the coat out, trim nails, give the face and feet a quick tidy, and check the ears. The whole appointment is usually 45 to 75 minutes.

If you book a bath and tidy and we spot something during the appointment — a small mat behind the ear, nails that turned out to need more work, an ear that needs a proper clean — we'll mention it before doing anything extra. No surprises on the bill.
Small dogs from £30, medium from £40, large or doodles from £50. Often the right choice for a Cocker Spaniel between full grooms, or a Labrador after the lake.

faqs.q: How is a bath and tidy different from a full groom?
faqs.a: No body clip or scissor finish. We bathe, dry, brush out, tidy face/feet/rear, do nails and ears — but we don't take length off the body. About £10 cheaper per size tier and ~30 minutes quicker.

faqs.q: Will the coat be smelling fresh?
faqs.a: Yes. We pick a shampoo for the coat type — gentle on skin, properly cleansing for muddy dogs, brightening for white coats. Towel and blow-dry leaves the coat fluffy, not damp.

faqs.q: Is this a good option for puppies after their intro groom?
faqs.a: Often yes — for short-coated puppies who've outgrown the puppy first groom but don't yet need a full body clip, a bath and tidy is a sensible step.

name: Nail Trim, Ear Clean & Tidy
summary: Quick maintenance visit between full grooms — nails, ears, face & feet tidy.
metaDescription: Quick dog nail trim, ear clean and tidy in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4. Nails from £10, nails + ears £15, full tidy £20. 15-30 minute appointments.
body: Sometimes you just need the nails done. Or the ears. Or a tidy round the eyes before they're rubbing on the cornea. A full groom isn't always the answer — and we'd rather do a quick maintenance visit than have you put it off because the cost of a full session feels like overkill.

Nails-only is the quickest appointment: 15 minutes, £10. Includes a careful look at the quick (the live part of the nail) so we never go too short. If your dog is nervous about feet, we'll work in shorter sessions and stop at whatever your dog is happy with.

Add an ear clean (£15 total) and we'll take a look inside the ear, gently clean the visible surface with a vet-approved solution, and flag anything that looks like a vet check might be sensible (we're groomers, not vets — but you get used to spotting infection early).

A full tidy (£20 total) is the maintenance lap — nails, ears, face, eyes, paw pads, sanitary trim. Usually 25 to 30 minutes. A great between-grooms option for dogs whose coats grow back quickly between proper full grooms.

faqs.q: How short can you cut my dog's nails?
faqs.a: As short as is safe. The 'quick' is the live blood vessel inside each nail — cut into it and it bleeds (a lot, briefly). We can see the quick on light nails and feel for it on dark ones, and we'll get as close as your dog will tolerate without going into it.

faqs.q: Can I bring my dog in just for nails between grooms?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Lots of customers do — saves the kitchen-floor disaster of trying it themselves. Quick appointments are easier to fit in too.

faqs.q: What if my dog hates having their feet touched?
faqs.a: We work slowly with treats and breaks. If a session ends with only two paws done, that's fine — book a follow-up at no extra cost. The goal is a dog who's calmer about feet, not a dog who's traumatised by the salon.

name: De-matting & Coat Recovery
summary: Careful, dog-first removal of mats. Severe matting assessed honestly on the day — coat health comes first.

tiers.label: Severe matting (clip-down)
tiers.note: Final price assessed in person — sometimes the kindest option is a fresh start.

includes: Aftercare guidance to keep mats away
metaDescription: Careful dog de-matting in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — coat recovery from £50. Severe matting honestly assessed; welfare always comes first.
body: Mats happen. Doodles, cocker spaniels, golden retrievers — any heavy-coated breed can develop matting between grooms, especially after wet walks or growth spurts in young dogs. We don't judge, we just help.
Light matting (small, surface-level tangles) we can usually work through during a normal full groom — we'll add a fee from £10 for the extra time. Brush, conditioner, gentle line-brushing, done.

Moderate matting (firmer, closer to the skin in patches) needs a dedicated de-matting session — from £50. We use de-matting spray and patient line-brushing, working in small sections, with breaks for your dog. This can take an hour or more, depending on coat condition.

Severe matting (pelting — when the coat has felted close to the skin) is harder. Brushing through a heavily pelted coat is genuinely painful for the dog, and not always safe — it can pull on skin and cause sores. The kindest, fastest option is usually a strip-clip down to a short, healthy length and start fresh. We'll always show you what we're seeing, talk it through, and never carry on if your dog is becoming distressed. From £60, often less for smaller dogs.

Either way, you'll leave with a clear plan for keeping the coat right between grooms — usually a more frequent groom cycle, plus a brushing routine that takes 3-5 minutes a day. We're happy to recommend a brush type for your specific coat.

faqs.q: Will it hurt my dog to remove the mats?
faqs.a: Mild matting, no — it's a slow, gentle process with conditioner. Severe matting, yes — pulling on pelted coat hurts and can damage skin. That's why we offer the strip-clip alternative for badly matted coats. Welfare always wins over aesthetics.

faqs.q: How do I stop matting happening again?
faqs.a: Two things — slightly more frequent grooms (every 5-6 weeks instead of 8), and a daily 3-minute brush with the right tool. We'll show you the tool and the technique before you leave.

faqs.q: Why is de-matting more expensive than a normal groom?
faqs.a: Time, and skill. A normal full groom is 1.5-3 hours. A heavily matted dog can take 2-4 hours plus a recovery period for the skin. The price reflects that — not the difficulty of brushing.

faqs.q: My dog won't stand still to be brushed at home. What do I do?
faqs.a: Start in tiny sessions — 30 seconds, lots of treats, increase gradually. We can talk you through the routine when you come in. Often the issue is the brush type, not the dog.

name: Hand Stripping
summary: Traditional hand stripping for wire-coated breeds — terriers, schnauzers, spaniels. Preserves coat colour & texture.
includes: Hand stripping in stages (gentle on the skin)
metaDescription: Traditional hand stripping in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — for wire-coated terriers, schnauzers and spaniels. Preserves coat colour and texture. From £50.
body: Hand stripping is the traditional method of grooming wire-coated breeds — Border terriers, Norfolk terriers, schnauzers, working cocker spaniels and many others. Instead of clipping the coat (which softens the texture and dulls the colour over time), hand stripping plucks dead hair out by hand, leaving the harder guard hairs intact. The coat keeps its proper texture, weather-resistance, and rich colour.

It's labour-intensive — usually 1.5 to 2.5 hours depending on size and how long the coat has been left — and skill matters. Done well, it's not painful for the dog (the dead hair lifts easily); done in a rush or to the wrong stage of growth, it can pull and irritate. Keith trained specifically in hand stripping at Mrs B's Grooming Academy.

We work in stages, taking breaks. Most dogs settle into it — many actively enjoy the rhythm. A coat that's been clipped for years can still be brought back to a proper stripped texture over two or three sessions, though it takes patience.

Pricing reflects time: small wire-coats (Border, Norfolk, Cairn) from £50; medium (Miniature Schnauzer, working Cocker, Lakeland) from £60; Standard Schnauzers and larger from £70. We'll always recommend the visit interval that suits your specific dog and how the coat is growing.

If you're unsure whether hand stripping is right for your dog, send us a photo of the coat — we can advise honestly. Some owners prefer the lower-maintenance clipped look, and that's a perfectly fine choice. We won't push you towards what's not right for you and your dog.

faqs.q: Does hand stripping hurt my dog?
faqs.a: Done correctly — no. We strip hair that's already at the end of its life cycle and ready to come out; it lifts with very little resistance. Done badly (or to coat at the wrong stage), it can pull. Skill and timing are everything.

faqs.q: How often should a stripped coat be done?
faqs.a: Most stripped breeds need a full strip every 8-12 weeks, with a light 'rolling' between if the coat blows quickly. We'll work out a schedule together based on how your specific dog's coat behaves.

faqs.q: My dog has been clipped for years. Can I still go back to hand stripping?
faqs.a: Often yes, but it takes patience. The first session might be more of a tidy than a true strip; the coat needs to grow through and re-set its texture. Usually 2-3 sessions to get to a properly stripped finish.

faqs.q: Is hand stripping the same price as a clipped groom?
faqs.a: Slightly more — it's significantly more time. Small wire-coats from £50, medium from £60, larger schnauzers from £70.
